summary.text: Christian Celeste Tate is a community organizer and consultant who describes himself as a democratic socialist. He is First Vice Chair of Brooklyn Community Board 4 and won the Democratic nomination for the open NY State Assembly District 54 seat by defeating incumbent Erik Dilan in the June 2026 primary; he also holds the Working Families Party line and is unopposed in November. According to his campaign, he is running on housing, immigration and public-safety platforms; this is his first run for public office.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, he grew up the son of a special education teacher and a small business owner, and his parents sent him and his sister to a private school.

After graduating with degrees in government and economics, he worked as a strategy consultant; his campaign website says that after the 2020 BLM protests in New York he dedicated himself to social change and now works as an impact consultant with philanthropists and nonprofits on poverty and inequality.

Organizes on housing with the East New York Community Land Trust, which his campaign website says includes knocking on doors, organizing rallies and standing with neighbors in court against predatory investors, and is North Brooklyn Chapter Chair of New York Communities for Change.

Served as East Brooklyn Field Coordinator for Zohran Mamdani's mayoral campaign and has led canvasses for Working Families Party candidates, according to his campaign website; City & State also reports he volunteered for the Mamdani campaign.
Is a member of NYC-DSA, where he helped lead the Afrosocialists and Socialists of Color Caucus, and of its North Brooklyn Branch's Community Solidarity Committee, according to his campaign website.

Is First Vice Chair of Brooklyn Community Board 4 and chairs its transportation committee; his campaign website says he helped write the board's 2025 Responsible Development Policy and advocated for accessibility at the Wilson Avenue subway station.

Has not previously held elected office. In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary he defeated incumbent Erik Dilan, 61.9% to 37.9%, per Ballotpedia; City & State reports he knocked on 4,000 doors during the campaign.

Ballotpedia lists endorsements from U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders and NYC-DSA, and City & State reports endorsements from the Democratic Socialists of America, the Working Families Party and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
